key_claims.claim: Four intra-amniotic categories in PPROM — sterile inflammation, microbial invasion without inflammation, microbial invasion with inflammation, and neither — have distinct gestational age distributions, microbial profiles, and neonatal outcomes.
The apparent treatment effect in GDM trials varies substantially depending on the composite endpoint chosen and the fetal growth standard applied.
Ovulation-based endometrial preparation for frozen embryo transfer is associated with higher live-birth rates and lower risk of hypertensive disorders of pregnancy compared to artificial cycles.
Genome sequencing identifies additional pathogenic variants in a meaningful proportion of nonimmune hydrops fetalis cases after nondiagnostic exome sequencing.
Neonatal outcomes differ meaningfully between persistent, resolved, and absent FGR, supporting trajectory-based rather than single-timepoint classification.
